title: Security playbooks on autopilot (SOAR)
summary: Routine threats get handled end to end in seconds: safe steps run automatically, risky ones wait for a person.

steps.label: malware detected
steps.title: Trigger
steps.text: A playbook starts automatically for every alert of this type. Same steps every time, no matter if it's 3 a.m.

steps.label: lookup hash
steps.title: Enrich automatically
steps.text: Read-only lookups are always safe to automate.
payload: Steals saved passwords and browser cookies.

steps.label: decide
steps.title: AI handles the judgement call
steps.text: Fixed rules cover the clear cases. The AI step reads the full context and picks a path from a fixed list, so it can't invent new actions.
payload: The model chooses; it can't add options.
"Known stealer, file not yet executed, single host"

steps.label: quarantine file
steps.title: Safe action: done automatically
steps.text: Quarantining one file is low-risk and easily undone, so it runs without waiting. Isolating a whole machine or a server would need approval.
payload: Reversible actions are the best candidates for automation.

steps.label: ticket + notify
steps.title: Close the loop
steps.text: A ticket records everything and the team is told what was done, so humans stay in charge without doing the busywork.
payload: "Info-stealer quarantined on HR-PC-07, no execution seen"
